title: Job Costing
outcomes: Explain the features and process of job costing.
Prepare a job cost card and price a job.
Treat spoilage and defectives in jobs.

meta.exam_tip: Read the profit basis carefully: "on cost" multiplies, "on selling price" divides.

concepts.title: Meaning, suitability and process of job costing
body: Job costing collects costs for each customer order (job) separately, because each job differs in specification, materials and time. It suits printing, furniture, repair workshops, interior decoration, machine tools and ship-building.

Process: a production order (job number) is issued; materials are drawn by requisitions quoting the job number; labour is booked by job time cards; overheads are absorbed at predetermined rates; on completion, the job cost card is totalled and compared with the price.
Work-in-progress at any date is the total of costs on all incomplete job cards.
concepts.analogy: Every job carries its own cost card, like a patient file in a hospital.
concepts.work: A printer quoting for 500 wedding cards opens job no. 2207 and charges paper, printing hours and binding to it.

concepts.title: Job cost card and pricing a job
body: The job cost card records direct materials (net of returns and transfers to other jobs), direct labour (hours × rate), direct expenses and overheads absorbed, often with an estimate column for comparison.
Overtime premium is charged to the job only if overtime was at the customer's request; otherwise it is an overhead. Idle time and normal losses are overheads.
Price is set by adding the desired profit: profit on cost (cost × (1 + markup)) or profit on selling price (cost ÷ (1 − margin)).
concepts.analogy: Get the cost right first; the price follows from the profit rule chosen.
concepts.work: Cost ₹80,000 with 20% profit on cost gives ₹96,000; with 20% on sale price, ₹1,00,000.

concepts.title: Work-in-progress, spoilage and defectives in jobs
body: Normal spoilage in a job is absorbed by good units, raising their cost; if the job is for a customer who specified tolerances, its cost stays in the job.
Abnormal spoilage is charged, after crediting scrap, to the Costing Profit and Loss Account.
Defectives that can be rectified: normal rectification cost goes to the job (if specific) or to production overheads; abnormal rectification cost goes to Costing P&L.
concepts.analogy: Expected losses belong to the product; unexpected ones belong to the period.
concepts.work: If a machine fault ruins 50 units in a job, their cost is written off, not loaded on the customer.

illustrations.title: Costing and pricing a custom order
illustrations.q: Job J-41 (a special conveyor for a client) required: materials issued ₹62,000, of which ₹4,000 was returned to stores; 120 normal labour hours and 40 overtime hours at ₹150 per hour, overtime at 150% being worked at the client's request for urgent delivery; direct expenses (hire of a crane) ₹3,000. Factory overheads are absorbed at ₹90 per labour hour; administration overheads at 10% of works cost. Prepare the job cost sheet and quote a price giving 20% profit on selling price.

head: Item
Working
rows: 120 × 150 + 40 × 225 (premium charged to job as requested by client)
solution.title: Job cost sheet — J-41

solution.text: Overtime premium is charged to the job only when overtime is worked at the customer's request; otherwise it is a production overhead.

checks.label: Direct labour including overtime premium at the job's request
Factory overheads at ₹90 per labour hour
Administration overheads at 10% of works cost
Price for 20% profit on selling price

illustrations.title: Spoiled units in a job
illustrations.q: A job of 10,000 identical components costing ₹30 each to the point of inspection had 700 spoiled units. Normal spoilage is 5% of input. Abnormal spoiled units realise ₹1,200 as scrap. How are normal and abnormal spoilage treated?

head: Item
Treatment
rows: Cost borne by good units in the job
Cost less scrap transferred to Costing P&L
solution.title: Spoilage in job costing

checks.label: Normal spoilage cost absorbed by good units (stays in job)
Abnormal spoilage loss to Costing P&L (net of scrap)

jobs.title: Tender pricing
jobs.situation: Sales wants a quote for a non-standard machine in two days.
steps: Add profit on the required basis and check competitiveness.
jobs.takeaway: A good quotation starts with a realistic estimated job cost card.

options: Each order is different and done to customer specification
mcqs.explain: Job costing traces costs to individual orders that differ. In practice: printing and repair shops use it.
mcqs.topic: Meaning, suitability and process of job costing

mcqs.q: Overtime premium paid because of a customer's urgent request is:
mcqs.explain: When the customer causes the overtime, the job bears it. General overtime is an overhead. In practice: document the request.
mcqs.topic: Job cost card and pricing a job

mcqs.q: Cost ₹60,000; profit 25% on selling price. Price:
mcqs.explain: 60,000 ÷ 0.75 = 80,000. In practice: 25% on cost would give ₹75,000.
mcqs.topic: Job cost card and pricing a job

mcqs.q: Abnormal spoilage in a job is charged to:
mcqs.explain: Abnormal losses are not part of product cost; net of scrap they go to Costing P&L. In practice: investigate their cause.
mcqs.topic: Work-in-progress, spoilage and defectives in jobs

options: Total cost on incomplete job cards
mcqs.explain: All costs booked to jobs not yet finished make up WIP. In practice: reconcile with WIP control.
mcqs.topic: Meaning, suitability and process of job costing

mcqs.q: Materials returned from a job to stores are:
options: Deducted from the job's material cost
mcqs.explain: Returns reduce the job's material cost via a material return note. In practice: transfers to other jobs use a transfer note.
mcqs.topic: Job cost card and pricing a job

mcqs.q: Normal rectification cost of defectives in a general production job is treated as:
mcqs.explain: Where defects are normal and not job-specific, rectification is spread through overheads. In practice: job-specific rectification goes to that job.
mcqs.topic: Work-in-progress, spoilage and defectives in jobs

mcqs.q: Labour cost is booked to jobs using:
mcqs.explain: Job time cards record hours worked on each job. In practice: idle time is booked separately.
mcqs.topic: Meaning, suitability and process of job costing

Overtime premium to job only if customer requested.

remember: WIP = cost on incomplete job cards.

viva.model: A specific order costing method in which costs are collected for each job or work order separately, as each differs from the others.

viva.q: What documents feed a job cost card?
viva.model: Material requisitions and return notes, job time cards and overhead absorption rates.
Charged to the job if worked at the customer's request; otherwise treated as production overhead.
Its cost, less scrap value, is transferred to the Costing Profit and Loss Account.

viva.q: Give examples of job costing industries.
viva.model: Printing, furniture making, repair workshops, interior decoration and heavy engineering.

cases.title: Fine Prints
cases.case: Fine Prints accepts job P-88: 1,000 brochures. Paper ₹18,000; ink ₹2,000; 30 labour hours at ₹200; machine overheads at ₹300 per machine hour for 12 hours; office overheads 20% of works cost. It wants 25% profit on cost.

mcqs.explain: Paper 18,000 + ink 2,000 + labour 6,000 = 26,000. In practice: ink is a direct material here.
mcqs.topic: Job cost card and pricing a job

mcqs.explain: 26,000 + 12 × 300 = 29,600. In practice: machine-hour rate suits printing.
mcqs.topic: Job cost card and pricing a job

mcqs.explain: 29,600 × 1.20 = 35,520. In practice: office overhead on works cost.
mcqs.topic: Job cost card and pricing a job

mcqs.explain: 35,520 × 1.25 = 44,400 (25% on cost). In practice: per brochure ₹44.40.
